steps.text: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C).
Blend pumpkin purée, tofu, pumpkin, sugar, cinnamon, salt, ginger, and cloves in a blender until smooth. Pour into pie crust.

Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce the heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and continue baking until a knife inserted into the center comes out clean, about 40 minutes more. Let cool completely before serving, about 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Tofu Pumpkin Pie
raw_recipe.description: Try this pumpkin pie made with tofu instead of eggs and dairy. Now all plant-based eaters at your holiday table can have your pie and eat it too!
raw_recipe.name: Tofu Pumpkin Pie

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C).
Blend pumpkin purée, tofu, pumpkin, sugar, cinnamon, salt, ginger, and cloves in a blender until smooth. Pour into pie crust.

Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce the heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and continue baking until a knife inserted into the center comes out clean, about 40 minutes more. Let cool completely before serving, about 1 hour.

review.reviewBody: This is great for vegans!! :)

I had to use firm tofu because our store was out of silken tofu. I threw everything into the Vitamix and it came out nice and smooth. I thought the pie had a distinct tofu taste-nothing whipped cream couldn't cover. I think next time I would add a bit more spice- maybe some nutmeg. I had to bake the pie 10 minutes longer then the recipe indicated. Good overall. A healthy option vs a protein bar :-)

I'm getting my wisdom teeth out tomorrow and can't eat solid foods for a week. I was looking for a recipe that wouldn't be too unpalatable or caloric and still was high in protein. This fit the bill! I used firm tofu (higher in protein), one can organic pumpkin puree, stevia instead of sugar (it's a 0 cal sweetener), and pumpkin spice. I had to add some almond milk. I've read it's better the second day, but I'm pleasantly surprised! I am actually looking forward to eating it! I divided it into four, and each serving is only 120cal, but packs a load of protein and vitamins!
I make this on Thanksgiving. I do change out the White Sugar for 1/4 cup of brown and 1/2 cup of coconut sugar. Turns out very yummy
A little runny so we had to broil it on low for ten minutes on the high rack. We substituted pumpkin spice for cloves and 1/4 cup of coconut sugar for 1/4 cup of pure sugar.

I also want to add something: I noticed someone's pie was really dark. Before you put it in the oven to bake, make a hood out of foil for your pie. It will protect it from getting scorched on the top. :)

If I hadn't made this pie myself, I don't think I would have guessed it had tofu in it! It was creamy and delicious. I couldn't find a 10.5-oz package of tofu, and I used one that was 12.3-oz. It worked fine. I left out the salt as we are on a low-sodium diet, and I used a store-bought deep-dish 9" crust. Exactly right! Thanks so much for this great pie.

Updated review: On the first day, this was edible, but not that great. The second day, however, this pie tasted very good! Definitely make this a day ahead of time to let the flavor improve!!
I do not have a blender, so I used a hand mixer, which I do NOT recommend if you're sharing this with others, simply because of the lack of visual appeal (it looked completely disgusting with beige chunks). I'm not vegan, and I do think regular pumpkin pie is better. I still might make this again, though, since it's so healthy and simple.

This was excellent! Used "soft" silken tofu and a low fat granola pie crust and reduced salt to 1/4 tsp but left everything else the same. Why would you want the eggs and dairy in a pumpkin pie when it can taste this good! Great recipe!

love this stuff! I used graham cracker crust last time I made it and while that sounds different it still turned out great. I only used cinnamon as that was all I had and it still came out wonderful. If you are finding this bland, you are not adding enough spice and sugar with the all important dash of salt. Also, VERY important to use SOFT not firm tofu, or it will have a weird texture, along with a very good food processor.

Very, very good! I made this for the first time this year for Thanksgiving (made the day before). It was very creamy, & no one knew it was made with tofu! (except for my mother - I made the recipe for her) No one else questioned that it tasted "different". However, the reason I gave it 4 stars & not 5 is because 1) both my mother & I thought it needed more of a real "pumpkin" flavor and 2)everyone noticed that the clove taste was a little strong. I think the next time I make it I'll use pumpkin pie spice instead and maybe a little extra pumpkin as well. Otherwise, I would absolutely recommend it to serve to anyone who can't have dairy. I'll be making it again.
This is permanently in my repertoire because the flavor is multi-dimensional, complex and exotic. I taste every spice in there. It is EASY. Pumpkin pie is my favorite and imho none compare to this.
We loved it. Made it for both Thanksgiving and Christmas. The refrigeration requirement just makes it a great make-ahead item. Very tasty.
This is definitely better the second day. I’ve been making this pie since 2004.
Surprisingly excellent in flavor and texture. Way yummy!

This was the first I tried this, it came out amazing! My husband loved it! No more traditional Pumpkin Pie for us..... I used coconut sugar instead of the process sugar. Had just the right hint of sweetness.
Everyone loved this! It was so easy to make & nobody even suspected that it was vegan or had tofu! I will def make again! Thanks
Great flavor!!
I made this exactly as written. I loved it! It set well and I thought the spices were perfect. I think this will be my go-to pumpkin pie recipe. Thanks for submitting Christopher!
This the second time I have made this recipe and it is consistently wonderful! The spices are perfect and the texture is lovely! Thanks!!
